(Elena sits on a park bench, clutching a folder, looking around nervously. Marcus approaches, umbrella in hand.)

MARCUS: Elena, my dear. I'm so glad you could make it. You must be freezing out here. (Offers her his umbrella)

ELENA: (Pulling the folder closer) I don't need your umbrella, Marcus. Let's just get this over with.

MARCUS: (Sitting down) Always so tense. Can't we have a civilized conversation? (Pauses) I know you're scared, Elena. But you have to understand - what you're doing, it's not just about you. There are so many people whose lives will be ruined if you go through with this.

ELENA: (Shaking her head) I don't believe that. Those people made their choices. Now it's time to face the consequences.

MARCUS: (Sighing) Oh, Elena. You're so idealistic. Don't you see? You're just a pawn in all of this. Those big-shot lawyers, they're the ones pulling the strings. They don't care about you. They'll use you and toss you aside the moment it's convenient.

ELENA: (Faltering) That's not true. I'm doing the right thing. I have to.

MARCUS: (Placing a hand on her arm) My dear, I know you think that. But what about your family? Your friends? Do you really want to put them through the hell of a drawn-out legal battle? The media scrutiny? The threats? (Shakes his head) I can make all of that go away. All you have to do is give me that folder.

ELENA: (Hesitating) I... I don't know. I just want to do the right thing.

MARCUS: (Squeezing her arm) I understand. Believe me, I do. But sometimes, the right thing isn't always the easiest thing. Think about the people you love. Think about your future. (Leans in) I can make this all go away, Elena. All you have to do is trust me.

(Elena looks down at the folder, her resolve visibly wavering.)

results.output:
HANS: (Slowly scooping Jello into his mouth) Hmm, this Jello is quite good today, don't you think, Clara?

CLARA: (Watching him intently) Yes, grandfather. It's your favorite, isn't it? Strawberry.

HANS: (Nods) Ah, yes. Strawberry. Always was my favorite. (Pauses) You know, I can't quite remember the last time we had Jello together. It's been... (Trails off, brow furrowing)

CLARA: (Leans forward) It's been a while, hasn't it? Too long. (Reaches across the table, placing her hand over his) I've missed our little chats.

HANS: (Glances down at her hand, then back up at her) Have you now? (Tilts his head) I must admit, my memory isn't what it used to be. These days, it's all a bit of a blur.

CLARA: (Squeezes his hand) I know, grandfather. But I'm here now. (Pauses, searching his face) Do you remember our last conversation? About the... mission?

HANS: (Brow creases, eyes narrowing) The mission? (Shakes his head slowly) I'm afraid I don't... (Trails off, gaze drifting)

CLARA: (Leans in closer) Think hard, Hans. It's important. (Lowers her voice) The one in Gdansk. You promised me you'd never forget.

HANS: (Holds her gaze for a long moment, then sighs) Ah, yes. Gdansk. (Nods slowly) How could I forget? (Looks down at the Jello, swirling his spoon) It's all so hazy these days, my dear. (Meets her eyes again) But I assure you, I haven't forgotten.

CLARA: (Visibly relaxes, a small smile playing on her lips) Good. I'm glad. (Squeezes his hand again) We have so much to discuss.
